case_number: Civil Appeal No. 404 of 2022 [Arising out of SLP(C) No. 21428 of 2019]
summary: The case involved a trademark infringement and passing off dispute over the use of the mark 'RENAISSANCE' in the hospitality sector. The appellant, Renaissance Hotel Holdings Inc., claimed exclusive rights over the mark 'RENAISSANCE' in Classes 16 and 42, asserting worldwide use since 1981 and in India since 1990. The respondents, operating hotels under 'SAI RENAISSANCE', defended on grounds of prior use, religious association with Sai Baba, lack of confusion due to distinct customer bases, and generic nature of the word 'renaissance'. The trial court found infringement in relation to registered trademarks but denied damages. The High Court set aside the trial court's decision, citing lack of transborder reputation, no deceptive similarity due to different service standards, and absence of unfair advantage. The Supreme Court granted leave to appeal, examining issues of trademark distinctiveness, reputation, and likelihood of confusion.
final_judgment: Leave granted; appeal to proceed on merits.
